naming: Every loader builds its YamlDotNet IDeserializer with new DeserializerBuilder().WithNamingConvention(CamelCaseNamingConvention.Instance).IgnoreUnmatchedProperties().Build(). A C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. Dictionary keys are never renamed by the convention. Enum-like string values are parsed case-insensitively; some (like load.mode) additionally strip - and _ before matching, confirmed per-case in the file-flow census (docs/reference/flow/keys.json), not assumed for these new document kinds.

keys.default: null (unset); coalesces to "default" (CatalogPipeline.DefaultBatch) at query time via the same generic catalog/run-list path used by every other flow kind, while the stored catalog row and the run record keep null
keys.description: Optional grouping label, consumed the same way as the file flow's batch but sourced from a different DTO (StoredProcedureYaml.Batch, not FlowYaml.Batch). Normalized to null via YamlDocumentParts.NullIfBlank and bound onto StoredProcedureFlow.Batch (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlStoredProcedureFlowLoader.cs:104). Consumed in three places: (1) the lineage collector stamps it on the flow's LineageFlowNode for kind 'sp' (src/SqlFlow.Lineage/Collection/FlowSetCollector.cs:148), which catalog sync projects onto the CatalogPipeline row exactly as for every other document kind (src/SqlFlow.Catalog/CatalogSync.cs:234-242); (2) StoredProcedureFlowRunner.BuildRecord copies it onto the run-history IngestionRunRecord.Batch field for every run (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:131); (3) the legacy full-mode host's RunStoredProcedureBatchAsync loads every stored-procedure flow sharing a Batch value from the legacy flw.StoredProcedure control-database table and runs them as one ordered sequence gated by onErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/FullMode/FullModeIngestionHost.cs:202-218); that path reads the legacy table rather than the YAML file, but is the same grouping concept.

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.

keys.description: Deployment lifecycle of the flow: 'production' (the default when absent) or 'development'. No consumer reads it back: it is not carried onto the LineageFlowNode the lineage collector builds for kind 'sp' (src/SqlFlow.Lineage/Collection/FlowSetCollector.cs:139-158), and StoredProcedureFlowRunner never references it; it is retained on the model purely for round-tripping and inspection of the flow definition.

Unique, human-readable identifier of the stored-procedure flow. Validated and trimmed by the shared YamlDocumentParts.RequireFlowName(y.Name, "a stored-procedure flow", source) (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlStoredProcedureFlowLoader.cs:80; helper at src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:231-233): unlike the file flow's own 'name' (FlowYaml.Name), whose loader does not trim it, every non-file document trims this value. The trimmed name becomes StoredProcedureFlow.SysAlias verbatim, the legacy mandatory SysAlias (src/SqlFlow.Core/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlow.cs:22), and seeds the flow's positive 31-bit int FlowId through YamlDocumentParts.StableFlowId: BitConverter.ToInt32(FlowIdentity.FromName(name).ToByteArray(), 0) & 0x7FFFFFFF (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:237-238), so renaming the flow changes its identity. Consumers use SysAlias/FlowId verbatim: the run.start log text "stored procedure '<SysAlias>' (flow <FlowId>): EXEC <Procedure.QualifiedName> on '<Server>'" and the run-history record's SysAlias field (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:56-57,132), DocumentExecutionResult.FlowName and the run-history folder name (src/SqlFlow.Execution/DocumentExecutor.cs:324-330), and the lineage collector's LineageFlowNode.Name for kind 'sp' (src/SqlFlow.Lineage/Collection/FlowSetCollector.cs:148), which catalog sync keys the pipeline row on the same way as every other document kind.

keys.description: Legacy batch-continuation flag (flw.StoredProcedure.OnErrorResume), bound as y.OnErrorResume ?? true onto StoredProcedureFlow.OnErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlStoredProcedureFlowLoader.cs:108; model default also true, src/SqlFlow.Core/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlow.cs:30). Documented in samples/sp/refresh-marts.flow.yaml's commented example as "batch behavior when this flow fails". In the YAML/without-database execution path traced here it is currently not consulted by anything: StoredProcedureFlowRunner.RunAsync always executes its one EXEC unconditionally and never branches on flow.OnErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs), and a flowType: batch document running this flow as a member gates wave continuation on the BATCH document's own onError/ignoreErrors settings instead of a member's onErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.Orchestration/BatchOrchestrator.cs:127-134). Its one confirmed live consumer is the legacy full-mode host, which loads stored-procedure flows from the legacy flw.StoredProcedure control-database table (a separate schema from the YAML/catalog path) and runs a same-Batch set sequentially, breaking out of the loop as soon as one flow's result is unsuccessful and OnErrorResume is false (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/FullMode/FullModeIngestionHost.cs:202-218).

keys.description: Alias of an invoke declared under the document's own invokes: block, run after the procedure EXECs successfully. Resolved and validated at parse time by YamlInvokeParts.ResolveHookAlias(y.PostInvoke, "postInvoke", invokes, source) (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlStoredProcedureFlowLoader.cs:109; helper at src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlInvokeParts.cs:200-216), which trims the value and requires it to already be a key of the invokes dictionary parsed from the SAME document; there is no separate flw.Invoke registry lookup on the without-database path. The resolved alias becomes StoredProcedureFlow.PostInvokeAlias (src/SqlFlow.Core/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlow.cs:32). At run time StoredProcedureFlowRunner runs the hook only after the procedure's EXEC has already succeeded, immediately before the run is reported successful: it logs an 'invoke.post' event and calls IInvokeRunner.RunByAliasAsync(flow.PostInvokeAlias.Trim(), ct) (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:64-68); a failed EXEC never reaches this step, so postInvoke never fires for a failing procedure run. If the hook itself throws, for instance because the referenced invoke ran and failed without its own onErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.Core/Invoke/IInvokeRunner.cs:60-64), that exception is caught by the SAME outer try/catch as the EXEC, so a procedure call that already committed is retroactively reported as a FAILED stored-procedure run, Success false with Error set to the invoke's failure message (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:54-111). The without-database composition (WithoutDatabaseStoredProcedure.BuildRunner via WithoutDatabaseInvokeRunner.Build) wires a real DefaultInvokeRunner whenever the document declares at least one invoke, which postInvoke's own parse-time check guarantees whenever postInvoke is set; it falls back to NullInvokeRunner, which raises a clear configuration error instead of silently skipping, only in the case, unreachable for a valid postInvoke, of a document with no invokes at all (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Invoke/WithoutDatabaseInvoke.cs:14-22; src/SqlFlow.Core/Invoke/IInvokeRunner.cs:20-31).

keys.description: The three-part [Database].[Schema].[Procedure] name to EXEC, e.g. DW.dbo.usp_RefreshMarts (samples/sp/refresh-marts.flow.yaml) or SqlFlowCatalogTests.demo.usp_BuildOrderFact (samples/lineage-demo/30-build-order-fact.flow.yaml). Parsed by RelationalObject.Parse via YamlDocumentParts.ParseQualifiedObject(raw, "procedure.object", source) (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlStoredProcedureFlowLoader.cs:93-95,107; parser at src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/RelationalObject.cs:20-48): the string is split on '.' respecting bracket-quoting (an inner ']' escaped as ']]'), and the rightmost three parts become Database/Schema/Name, so a stray leading fourth part such as a server prefix is silently dropped rather than rejected. The parsed object becomes StoredProcedureFlow.Procedure, a RelationalObject (src/SqlFlow.Core/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlow.cs:28), whose QualifiedName re-brackets and re-escapes each part as [Database].[Schema].[Name] (RelationalObject.cs:18). At run time StoredProcedureFlowRunner builds a SqlCommand whose CommandText is exactly this QualifiedName, with CommandType.StoredProcedure and no SqlParameters ever added, the parameter-less EXEC (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:114-119); the same QualifiedName is captured verbatim in the run's SQL trace as 'EXEC <QualifiedName>;' (StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:59) and in the run.start log line (StoredProcedureFlowRunner.cs:56-57). Because the grammar has no field for arguments, a procedure requiring mandatory parameters fails at the database with SQL Server's own missing-parameter error, not a SQLFlow-level one. For lineage, the parsed object is recorded as a 'Requires' fact, not Reads/Writes, on the resolved server: the flow only declares that it needs the procedure, not what the procedure itself reads or writes, unless a connected sync (db sync --connect) derives that separately (src/SqlFlow.Lineage/Collection/FlowSetCollector.cs:154-156; samples/lineage-demo/30-build-order-fact.flow.yaml).
